records.sourceAnchor: MCA SPICe+ Part A and Part B, linked services, V3 portal boundary and official incorporation route
observations: The current MCA portal confirms that company-incorporation work is handled in the V3 environment and continues to publish V3 SPICe+ and linked-filing guidance. UdyamVeda must not route users to legacy V2 filing instructions.

The official instruction kit distinguishes SPICe+ Part A for name reservation from Part B for incorporation details. Part A may be submitted separately for name reservation or together with Part B; Part B and linked forms become available after an approved Part A SRN when name reservation is filed separately.

The official FAQ describes Part B as covering company registration/CIN, Section 8 licensing where applicable, DIN allotment, PAN/TAN allocation and optional GSTIN application. The exact current linked-service sequence and scope must be rechecked against the live V3 form before publication.

The FAQ also describes AGILE-PRO-S and linked services such as bank-account opening, EPFO, ESIC and selected state services. These are preparation dependencies, not proof that every service applies to every company or that later statutory compliance thresholds are satisfied.

UdyamVeda may collect a preparation checklist and validate completeness, but the applicant or authorised professional must use the applicant's own MCA account, business-user role, DSC and declarations. UdyamVeda must not impersonate the applicant or retain signing credentials.

This record is a registration workflow, not a grant or financial benefit. Any filing fee, state stamp duty, name-reservation validity, resubmission condition or processing expectation must be versioned from current MCA evidence rather than inferred from the older FAQ.

records.sourceAnchor: SPICe+ Part B PAN/TAN allocation, Income Tax Department tax-identity handoff, current portal verification and 2026 legal-transition boundary
observations: The MCA SPICe+ FAQ places PAN/TAN allocation within the incorporation-time linked service route for eligible company applications. This does not mean every entity or every applicant should use the same route.

The current Income Tax portal remains the authoritative tax-identity handoff and provides PAN/TAN service and verification boundaries. UdyamVeda should guide users to the official route when incorporation-time allocation is unavailable, incomplete or requires a separate application.

The Income Tax Department's 2026 transition guidance must be used to distinguish existing PAN/TAN continuity from fresh applications and to confirm the applicable current forms. The record must not hard-code historical forms, fees or processing times without current evidence.

PAN, TAN, OTPs, DSCs and identity credentials remain applicant-controlled sensitive data. UdyamVeda may validate document presence and explain the next step, but must not request OTPs, impersonate the taxpayer or store identity numbers unless a separately approved workflow requires it.

PAN/TAN allocation is an administrative identity outcome, not a subsidy, grant or guaranteed processing result. The recommendation and application model must show the official handoff and unresolved status separately.
reviewFollowUps: Confirm the current TAN-specific form, fee, eligibility, signing and correction route separately from PAN.
Confirm live SPICe+ and Income Tax handoff behavior for each supported entity type and for failed or delayed TAN allocation.
Reconcile document and identity requirements against current Income Tax forms and 2026 notifications.
Verify that the product's consent, masking, deletion and credential-handling controls satisfy the privacy boundary before enabling document extraction.
